subject: English Language

questions.prompt: What problem affects species and ecosystems? (A noise pollution, B water pollution, C air pollution, D land pollution, E gas pollution)
steps: The included page 5 script begins with this problem.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does polluted water affect? (A plants and organisms, B animals, C oceans, D plants, E bacteria)
steps: The script explicitly names these groups.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Plants and organisms living in water.

questions.prompt: Which activity is a major cause of pollution in the script? (A business, B wood, C water, D air, E agriculture)
steps: The script explains fertiliser runoff from crops.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which planet has liquid water on its surface in the script? (A other planets, B Mars, C Jupiter, D Earth, E Pluto)
steps: The script identifies Earth; this concerns stable surface liquid water.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How much daily water does the script state? (A 6 L, B 4 L, C 3 L, D 7 L, E 15 L)
steps: Read the specified amount as the passage answer; individual needs vary and this is not a prescribed intake for every child.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. Approximately 3 litres, according to the script.

questions.prompt: Ogweno shared land ___ four sons. (A among, B between, C beside, D besides, E within)
steps: Among expresses distribution within a group.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Among (expected school answer). Between is also used for distinct individual parties.

questions.prompt: Food was ___ delicious that he wanted it daily. (A very, B too, C so, D extremely, E as)
steps: So...that links degree and result.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The train ___ late three times this week. (A was being, B is, C has been, D would be, E has being)
steps: This week is a continuing period; use present perfect.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Build a ___ school. (A girls, B girl's, C girls's, D girls', E girl)
steps: The plural possessive places the apostrophe after s.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The deer was ___ when the hunter saw it. (A died, B has died, C dies, D dead, E die)
steps: Was dead describes its state.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Joan will be late unless she prepares early. Fill the conjunction from his, adjective, cleverest, two, twice, her, unless, clever, adverb.
steps: Unless means if she does not.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: We ate chicken and chips ___ a month.
steps: Twice means two times; two alone cannot modify a month this way.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: He is the ___ and hardworking pupil in class.
steps: The comparison with the class uses the superlative.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The young princess ordered ten burgers for herself. Identify the part of speech of the underlined word using adjective/adverb from the bank. No target underline is visible.
steps: Young describes the noun princess.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Adjective, if young is the intended target; young describes princess. No word is visibly underlined, so the exact target is not prescribed.

questions.prompt: The book belongs to Nurya, so it is ___ her book (printed).
steps: Her goes directly before book; inserting her in the printed blank would duplicate it.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Intended bank word: her. Corrected sentence: It is her book. As printed, no extra possessive is needed before the existing her.

questions.prompt: Match cloth worn around the neck/shoulders/head: A minutes, B scarf, C theatre, D club, E screech, F debate.
steps: A scarf is the described cloth garment.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match a record of a formal meeting.
steps: Minutes record what a meeting discusses and decides.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match a thick-ended heavy stick used as a weapon.
steps: Club is the described stick.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match the sound of vehicle brakes.
steps: Brakes may make a sharp screech.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match a place for dramatic performances.
steps: A theatre hosts drama.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The pen belongs to me. It is ___. Bank: ours, mine, by, in order, and, except, hers, his, your, on, with.
steps: Mine is the possessive pronoun for the speaker.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Nasra comes to school ___ bus.
steps: By bus identifies the means of transport.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: We eat ___ to survive.
steps: To is already printed; in order completes in order to.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Catherine is both tall ___ fat.
steps: Use both...and.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Every pupil works hard ___ you.
steps: Except excludes the stated person from the group.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: On which day did the football tragedy occur?
steps: The opening gives this day and period.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who scored the only goal?
steps: The passage says she scored after receiving Kipanya's cross.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What do people obtain from the well?
steps: A well is used to obtain water; this is an inference, not an explicit sentence in the passage.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Name one person who died in the well.
steps: The story states that all three pushed into the well drowned.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Miriam, Chiku or the referee (any one).

questions.prompt: Which game was being played?
steps: The opening identifies a football match.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order A-E: The scream came from outside her house.
steps: Locate the sound after she wakes.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: She saw a lion dragging a person from a house.
steps: This is what she sees after looking out.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Last month a terrible event happened in a village.
steps: Introduce the event first.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: She left her bed and looked through the window.
steps: Looking follows hearing the scream.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Mama Amina was sleeping until a scream woke her.
steps: Introduce her situation after the event opening.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Listening: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Grammar: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Vocabulary: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Comprehension and composition: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: Standard Six Midterm Exams August 2024 By MESP Tanzania

limitations: Numbering: Listening and bank both print 1; multiple-choice and matching both print 2. Unique labels retain all 35 parts.
1-Bank(v): A duplicated her makes the printed blank defective.
1-Listen(v): 3 litres is the script claim, not universal child-specific health advice.
1-Bank(iv): Target underline is absent. Young is an adjective and the most plausible bank-compatible target.
